question_text: Q1. What is the primary objective of a security architecture?

options.label: B
options.text: Define how security controls protect organizational assets and systems

question_text: Q2. Which principle assumes that no user or device should be trusted by default?
Q3. What does the principle of least privilege mean?

options.label: B
options.text: Users should receive only the access necessary to perform their tasks

question_text: Q4. Which security architecture strategy uses multiple layers of security controls?
Q5. Which component is primarily responsible for controlling access between trusted and untrusted networks?
Q6. What is network segmentation primarily used for?

options.label: B
options.text: Limiting the spread of attacks and unauthorized access

question_text: Q7. In a Zero Trust architecture, authentication should generally be performed:

options.label: A
options.text: Only when a user first joins the organization

options.label: B
options.text: Continuously or whenever access context changes

question_text: Q8. Which technology is commonly used to provide an additional authentication factor?
Q9. What is the primary purpose of Identity and Access Management (IAM)?

options.label: A
options.text: Manage identities and control access to resources

question_text: Q10. Which security control is most appropriate for limiting lateral movement after an attacker compromises one system?
Q11. What is the main purpose of a DMZ in network security architecture?

options.label: B
options.text: Host publicly accessible services while isolating them from the internal network

question_text: Q12. Which architecture principle requires systems to remain secure even when individual security controls fail?
Q13. Which of the following is an example of data at rest?

options.label: C
options.text: Data being transferred through a network

question_text: Q14. Which technology is commonly used to protect data in transit?
Q15. What is the primary purpose of encryption in a security architecture?
Q16. Which security principle recommends disabling unnecessary services and functionality?
Q17. What is threat modeling used for?

options.label: A
options.text: Identifying potential threats and designing appropriate mitigations

question_text: Q18. Which framework is commonly associated with identifying threats using concepts such as tactics and techniques used by attackers?
Q19. What is the primary function of a SIEM system?

options.label: B
options.text: Collect, correlate, and analyze security logs and events

question_text: Q20. Which security control can detect and potentially block malicious network traffic?
Q21. What is the difference between IDS and IPS?

options.label: A
options.text: IDS detects; IPS can detect and actively prevent or block

options.label: C
options.text: IDS authenticates users; IPS stores passwords

question_text: Q22. Which architecture is most appropriate for isolating sensitive workloads from general corporate systems?
Q23. In cloud security architecture, the shared responsibility model means that:

options.label: A
options.text: The cloud provider is responsible for everything

options.label: B
options.text: The customer is responsible for everything

options.label: C
options.text: Security responsibilities are divided between the provider and customer

options.label: D
options.text: Neither party is responsible for security

question_text: Q24. Which principle is particularly important when designing APIs securely?

options.label: A
options.text: Authenticate and authorize every sensitive request

options.label: B
options.text: Allow anonymous access to all endpoints

question_text: Q25. What is a security baseline?

options.label: A
options.text: A minimum set of security configurations and controls that systems should meet

options.label: B
options.text: A backup copy of a database

question_text: Q26. Which approach provides security controls closest to the workload or application being protected?
Q27. What is the primary security benefit of microsegmentation?

options.label: B
options.text: It limits communication between individual workloads or segments

options.label: C
options.text: It removes the need for authentication

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminates the need for monitoring

question_text: Q28. Which architectural concept focuses on designing systems so that security failures do not expose the entire system?
Q29. Which of the following is the BEST approach for protecting privileged administrator accounts?

options.label: A
options.text: Share one administrator account among employees

options.label: B
options.text: Use privileged access management, MFA, and least privilege

question_text: Q30. Which combination BEST represents a strong modern security architecture?

options.label: C
options.text: Zero Trust + least privilege + segmentation + MFA + continuous monitoring
